issues.description: The Bitmap24 class constructor declaration in the template header declares a three-parameter constructor (int i_width, int i_height, int depth), but the implementation defines a two-parameter constructor (int p_width, int p_height). The solution's header and implementation both use the two-parameter constructor. This mismatch will cause compilation/linker errors and confuses students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header's constructor signature match the implementation and the solution: change Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). Ensure all declarations and implementations (template and solution) use the same two-parameter constructor.

issues.description: Constructor signature/parameter naming for Bitmap24 differs between template and solution: the template header declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) and the solution header declare a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). This mismatch (the extra 'depth' parameter name) creates confusion about the intended constructor API and may lead students to be unsure which signature to implement or expect, and could cause compilation/linking surprises when matching declarations to definitions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration consistent across artifacts. Either remove the unused 'depth' parameter from the template header (change to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);) to match the implementation, or update the implementation and solution header to include and document the 'depth' parameter if it is intended. Prefer removing 'depth' in the template header to match the implementation and solution for minimal disruption.
